program: Low-income primary care and medication access
priceScope: Conditional annual whole-recipient cost divided by a limited modeled local channel; not a verified marginal gift offer or complete portfolio EV

what: Christ Clinic provides primary, preventive and specialty care to uninsured and underinsured people in the Katy area.
Its Total Care program combines chronic disease care, medication assistance, laboratory services and limited behavioral health treatment.
Express Care, employer memberships and the church-linked 2535 initiative provide additional routes to accessible care.
strengths: Current eligibility and service descriptions are specific about low-income access.
Three original annual returns support a consistent recognized-expense series and verified recipient identity.
Medication assistance and multidisciplinary care offer plausible health and household resource mechanisms.
reservations: No current unique completed treatment cohort or causal outcomes were verified.
All numerical health and resource response parameters are unsupported local priors.
Unrecognized donated clinical resources and marginal funding capacity remain unresolved.

sections.what: Christ Clinic provides primary, preventive and specialty care to uninsured and underinsured people in the Katy area. Its Total Care program combines chronic disease care, medication assistance, laboratory services and limited behavioral health treatment. Express Care, employer memberships and the church-linked 2535 initiative provide additional routes to accessible care.
sections.monitoring: Current primary sources describe services, not unique annual completions or causal improvements. Request unique adults and households, repeated visits, clinical follow-up, medication adherence, alternative care use and recipient-specific net household expenses. Verify membership revenue, current partner capacity and whether new donations expand appropriate care rather than replace public or employer funding.
sections.qualitative: Current eligibility and service descriptions are specific about low-income access. Three original annual returns support a consistent recognized-expense series and verified recipient identity. Medication assistance and multidisciplinary care offer plausible health and household resource mechanisms. No current unique completed treatment cohort or causal outcomes were verified. All numerical health and resource response parameters are unsupported local priors. Unrecognized donated clinical resources and marginal funding capacity remain unresolved. Original FY2024 EIN 90-0789318 and Katy address identify the recipient. Official donation route is checked, not a transaction or restriction. The 2535 initiative is part of this recipient, not a separate benefit added to the cohort.
sections.cost: The conditional limited-channel reference is $19.27 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents, with 0.933873 clinical QALYs and -0.039834 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.005189 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not verified next-gift response. Annual recognized recipient cost is $1,723,027. The 1,000 annual patient opportunities are a judgment; .8 distinct household share and .4 counterfactual annual response yield 320 household proxies, including 64 judged clinical improvers. Utility .03 for .5 years is a weak morbidity hypothesis, not an empirical average or cardiovascular/mortality conversion. Resource success .3 is independent of clinical success. $300 otherwise-paid care avoided is a hypothetical actual payment avoided after alternative-provider substitution, not retail care value; positive overlap .5 and full $50 incremental travel, work disruption or contribution burden give success households $100 net and other households −$50. A single joint household log uses $20,000 annual consumption and one welfare-equivalent adult per household. Gross wages, ordinary survivor earnings and retail medication value are excluded. Positive components alone receive overlap reduction; negative resources and all union harms remain full. ResourceYears is a fraction of one year's gain, not recurrent lifetime savings. Provider/payer costs are separate from participant costs; central external zero is unknown-neutral, not evidence of zero or complete world net benefit. Whole annual recipient cost supports a narrow conditional numerator; complete portfolio and marginal funding EV remain unknown.
sections.funding: Original recognized expenses are FY2024 $1,723,027, FY2023 $2,297,861 and FY2022 $1,912,440. No populated netted event, inventory or rental expense field was recovered in these originals; this is not a claim that unrecognized donated professional resources cost nothing. FY2024 program service revenue $482,099 indicates patient/employer payment mechanisms alongside donations. All recognized expense is retained; additional partner opportunity costs are separately stressed. No arbitrary match is applied to the full denominator or annual numerator.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Katy delivery is within the Houston MSA; .98 patient share is a judgment, not measured county distribution.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Alternative charity clinics, FQHC/public care, insurance eligibility, household payments and employer funding replacement; additional annual care response remains a prior.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional appropriate care and finite symptom relief in a judged annual patient cohort; visits and medicine retail values are not outcomes.
